chunks: And Pharaoh, the one of the pegs.

key_terms.ذِي الْأَوْتَادِ: The one of the pegs, an epithet denoting power or a specific tribe
key_terms.فِرْعَوْنَ: Pharaoh, the tyrannical ruler of Egypt

ai.seo_question: Who is Pharaoh Dhi al-Awtad in the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, 'Dhi al-Awtad' (Possessor of the Pegs) is interpreted both literally as having many sons or strongholds and metaphorically as possessing great power or using pegs for torture, emphasizing Pharaoh's absolute tyranny. This epithet appears in Surah Al-Fajr (89:10-12) alongside the tribe of Thamud, linking the two major archetypes of arrogance in Islamic history. The reference serves as a warning against divine retribution for those who oppress the believers, a theme central to Shia historical consciousness regarding the Umayyads and Abbasids.
